checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The routing policy declares deterministic verification depth, required evidence categories, and optional checks for light, standard, and strict; each profile has a materially different projection.

Profile selection and quality dispatch consume the profile projection: light is focused, standard adds project verification and reference/test-weakening checks, and strict adds the full quality graph plus strict evidence; release escalation remains separate and automatic.

Mandatory controls remain invariant across profiles: scope, trust/security, required lifecycle checks, evidence integrity, and fail-closed unknown/invalid override behavior cannot be disabled or downgraded.

Focused tests prove profile monotonicity, profile-specific depth/evidence/optional-check projections, non-release strict behavior, release escalation, and rejection of attempts to remove mandatory controls.

Canonical English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese governance-profile references describe the profile effect, mandatory-control floor, optional-check boundary, and release distinction without claiming runtime orchestration or performance improvement.
guidelines: Profiles may reduce optional verification cost only; they may not disable security, scope, required controls, mandatory lifecycle gates, or evidence integrity.
Risk can escalate automatically but cannot be lowered by explicit input or incomplete human override evidence.
Keep release as an operation-specific strict escalation rather than a fourth governance profile.
Keep profile projections deterministic, auditable, and documented in all supported reference locales.
Do not add scheduler/runtime orchestration or performance claims to this Work Item.

intent.problem: The repository already routes work to Light, Standard, and Strict quality targets, but the profile effect is not explicit enough in the machine-readable verification and evidence contract. Operators cannot reliably see which checks are required versus optional, and a future optimization could accidentally lower mandatory controls.
constraints: Use only light, standard, and strict as Governance Profile values; release is a separate operation escalation.
Make depth, evidence requirements, and optional checks deterministic and auditable.
Preserve mandatory security, scope, required controls, lifecycle gates, and fail-closed behavior at every profile.
Keep implementation within routing/verification policy, quality dispatch, tests, and canonical profile documentation.
intent.rationale: An explicit profile projection makes cost and evidence tradeoffs reviewable while preserving an invariant mandatory-control floor. This enables later performance work to optimize optional work without weakening trust.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Light profile uses focused verification while preserving mandatory controls
scenarioCoverage.expected: Light has focused depth, smaller optional set, and the same mandatory scope/security/lifecycle floor as other profiles.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused routing and projection tests for a documentation-only change.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Standard profile adds project verification and evidence
scenarioCoverage.expected: Standard is full project depth and adds project-test/reference/test-weakening evidence without release checks.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused policy and Make dispatch tests for ordinary source/test changes.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Strict profile requires full governance and cannot be lowered
scenarioCoverage.expected: Strict requires the full graph and strict evidence; invalid or incomplete lower-profile requests fail closed.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run monotonicity, override, mandatory-floor, and strict routing tests.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Release operation escalates independently of profile intensity
scenarioCoverage.expected: Release paths/claims add release_preflight and distribution, while non-release Strict does not acquire release checks.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run release derivation and non-release strict focused tests.
